statement:
Research objective: Estimate how switch frequency in matchup data relates to opponent efficiency, team by team, and whether high-switch teams concede different shot types.

Data: 2026-27 NBA regular season from 2026-10-20 to 2027-01-31 (development period), plus 2022-23 to 2024-25 seasons. The 2025-26 season is not provided. Fields: defensive matchups (off/def player, matchup_minutes, partial_possessions, switches_on, player_points, fg_made, fg_attempted); play-by-play actions (actionType, subType, clock, period, teamId, personId, scoreHome/scoreAway, shotDistance, xLegacy/yLegacy, shotResult, shotValue, description).
Unit of analysis to consider: team-game switch counts (about 1422 expected in the development period).
What would count as a meaningful finding: A relationship between switching and opponent shot mix that replicates.
Validation: claims are tested on games from 2027-01-31 to 2027-04-12, which are sealed until every claim is registered. Planned approach: Re-estimate the team-level relationship on validation games.

Register at most three claims. Each claim needs an estimand, a direction, a pre-specified test with a pass rule, and an analysis script that runs unchanged on the validation data.
permitted_memory: full history (all 384 records); no record uses 2026-27 data
